feature_candidates.description: Bucket video duration into intervals with an explicit zero/NA bucket, fed as an item-side categorical embedding.
feature_candidates.expected_impact: Captures non-linear duration effects and stabilizes zero-duration rows; likely improves long_view ranking.
feature_candidates.implementation_scope: Preprocess video feature table once; map duration to bucket id; add to item embedding lookup in model config.
feature_candidates.leakage_risk: Low; duration is a static video property, not a period aggregate.
feature_candidates.name: duration_bucket_na

feature_candidates.description: Per-video long_view/finish propensity computed only from train log exposures, normalized by duration to mitigate popularity bias.
feature_candidates.expected_impact: Strong item-side signal for within-user ranking if computed on train-only and carefully normalized.
feature_candidates.implementation_scope: Compute from train interactions with deduplication; join to video table and add as scalar item feature; validate on valid only.
feature_candidates.leakage_risk: Low if strictly train-only; high if using the leaky full-platform statistics table.
feature_candidates.name: train_only_video_longview_finish_rate

feature_candidates.description: Train-only user past long_view rate within video category or upload type, forming a user-category affinity feature.
feature_candidates.expected_impact: Personalizes category preference and improves ranking for users with stable past behavior.
feature_candidates.implementation_scope: Aggregate train log by user and video category to obtain ratio counts; use as auxiliary interaction feature outside main tab embedding.
feature_candidates.leakage_risk: Low if computed only from train rows and no validation-period data is used.
feature_candidates.name: user_history_category_longview_ratio

findings.implication: Tab should be a conditioning variable or used for negative sampling in BPR/group_softmax to reduce exposure bias.
findings.observation: Tab 4 has long_view rate 48.93% and tab 0 has 4.22%, with tab 1 at 38.61%, so intra-user tab context is highly discriminative.
findings.title: Tab strongly stratifies long_view

findings.implication: Duration-derived features must include an explicit NA/zero bucket rather than imputing or dropping these rows.
findings.observation: 239 videos have zero duration, affecting 24,076 train rows and creating a distinct missing/zero category.
findings.title: Zero-duration videos distort duration features

findings.implication: Features derived from it may encode future signals; use only with explicit leakage caveats or rely on train-only aggregates.
findings.observation: The video statistics table reflects full-platform aggregates over periods beyond the log span, with exposure ratio about 4,892:1 vs logged data.
findings.title: Video statistics table is leaky period aggregate

expected_artifacts: Correlation matrix of candidate features vs long_view within user groups.
Tab-stratified long_view rate by video duration bins.
Train-only user history feature summary (mean long_view per user, per video category).
EDA report listing top 10 feature hypotheses for BPR/group_softmax experiments.
feature_hypotheses: Video duration buckets and normalized play progress signals from the statistics table improve long_view ranking beyond static fields.
Per-video long_view propensity (e.g., duration-weighted finish rate) adds a strong item-side feature for BPR.
User past long_view ratio on similar video categories improves within-user ranking.
Negative sampling based on tab and time-of-day buckets reduces group_softmax bias.
leakage_risks: Video statistics table is full-platform period aggregate; features from it may leak future exposure signals.
Zero-duration videos (24k train rows) may distort duration-derived features if not handled with explicit NA buckets.
User history features may leak if computed over the validation period or full log rather than train-only.
Exact duplicate rows (15.6k) could inflate correlation if not deduplicated in EDA.
plan.objective: Plan one leakage-safe EDA pass to identify within-user long_view ranking signals that can be exploited by BPR or group_softmax families.
questions: Which video-side statistics (e.g., duration, play rate, finish rate) show the largest intra-user variance and correlate with long_view conditional on tab?
How does long_view rate vary by video duration buckets, especially for zero-duration videos?
Does the user's interaction history (likes, comments, follows) on the video's creator predict long_view?
Are there tab-specific video popularity thresholds that improve group_softmax negatives sampling?
required_inputs: Train and valid interaction logs with user_id, video_id, tab, hourmin, long_view labels.
Video feature table (duration, type, upload_type) and video statistics table (view counts, play duration aggregates).
Experiment history metrics for bpr_b01 and bpr_b02 as baselines.

report.recommended_next_focus: Run a BPR/group_softmax ablation adding duration bucket plus train-only user-history category affinity, conditioning negatives by tab, while keeping all statistics features train-only.
report.summary: EDA plan focuses on tab-stratified long_view by duration, zero-duration NA handling, train-only user-history propensities, and caveated video-stats features. BPR/group_softmax families should condition on tab and use deduplicated train rows.
ui_notes: Plot long_view rate vs duration bins separately for main tabs using train-only data.
Do not mix valid-period rows into EDA plots; 15.6k duplicated log rows should be deduplicated first.
Show bpr_b01 baseline primary 0.6033 (GAUC 0.6698, nDCG@5 0.5368) against the plan's target improvements.
